exposure: Sexual orientation (categorized as sexual minority, completely heterosexual, heterosexual with prior same-sex experience, mostly heterosexual, bisexual, and lesbian/gay subgroups)
cohort: The study included 102,298 singleton, live births from the Nurses' Health Studies 2 and 3, and the Growing Up Today Study.
finding: Sexual minority participants had higher risks of primary Cesarean birth than their completely heterosexual peers, with increases most pronounced among those identifying as heterosexual with prior same-sex experience.
mod_finding: Disparities in primary Cesarean birth risk by sexual orientation were more pronounced when labor was induced compared to spontaneous labor.
